description:
Redwood Inference is adding a new Dedicated Capacity feature: a controlled “burst capacity” option that allows dedicated customers to temporarily exceed their reserved baseline GPU allocation by borrowing from managed burst pools, while enforcing guardrails that protect neighbor workloads and preserve platform-wide SLOs.

Goals
- Provide a paid burst option for Dedicated customers that increases throughput during predictable peaks (batch jobs, launches, weekly traffic spikes) without requiring permanent over-provisioning.
- Protect non-bursting tenants and the broader fleet from noisy-neighbor effects via strict admission control, fairness, and circuit breakers.
- Make bursting observable, auditable, and supportable: clear dashboards, alerts, customer-visible reporting, and operational runbooks.
- Integrate with billing and packaging: metering burst usage, configurable limits, and contract/SLA language.

In-scope
- Burst pool architecture per region/hardware class (e.g., H100 us-east, L40S eu-west) with pool sizing policies.
- Admission control + guardrails: max burst ratio, per-tenant caps, cooldown windows, queue/backpressure behavior, and global fleet safety limits.
- Control plane APIs/config: enable burst for a tenant, set limits, and define priorities/tiering.
- Routing + data plane integration: capacity signals consumed by routing, deterministic policy evaluation, safe fallback when burst is denied.
- Observability: metrics for burst requests/denials, saturation, neighbor impact indicators (p95 latency deltas, tail amplification), and SRE alerting.
- Rollout plan: internal dogfood, limited beta customers, GA, then tuning.

Out of scope (initial release)
- Arbitrary cross-region bursting (initially burst is constrained within region).
- Customer-custom burst pools (initially shared Redwood-managed pools with strict segmentation).
- Complex reservation trading/spot-market behavior.

Key stakeholders
- Product (Dedicated): Lauren Bishop (program owner), plus Product Ops inputs for packaging.
- Platform Control Plane: Ethan Park (config APIs/policy evaluation), Benji Okafor, Jordan Lee.
- Fleet/Infrastructure: Vanessa Ortiz (fleet capacity ownership), Keiko Yamamoto (autoscaling + guardrails), Harish Reddy.
- Smart Routing: Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon, Elena Popov.
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant.
- Finance/Legal: Rishi Malhotra (unit economics + pricing), Laura Bennett (approvals), Michael Grant/Sofia Mendes (contract terms).
- GTM/CS: Stephanie Nguyen/Lukas Meyer (enablement), Rachel Kim/Miguel Santos (customer readiness and comms).

Phases & timeline (hypothetical)
- Discovery & design (2025-01 to 2025-02): requirements, pool model, guardrails, pricing/packaging proposal, security review.
- Implementation (2025-03 to 2025-04): control plane config + admission controller, routing hooks, metering, dashboards.
- Internal beta/dogfood (2025-05): enable for internal workloads + a few friendly Dedicated accounts; refine thresholds.
- GA rollout (2025-06): staged rollout by region/hardware; publish docs; sales enablement.
- Post-GA hardening (2025-07 onward): tuning fairness, improving prediction signals, incident learnings folded into runbooks.

Primary deliverables
- PRD + design spec + ADRs (pool model, admission control semantics).
- Implementation PRs across monorepo (control plane, routing, infra, observability, docs).
- SRE runbooks/alerts and a game day plan.
- Pricing/packaging guidance + customer-facing enablement and contract language stubs.

Constraints & risks
- Must not regress non-burst SLOs; enforce hard “fleet safety” caps and fast rollback.
- Billing accuracy: burst metering must be precise and reconciled with per-tenant configs.
- Capacity realities: pool sizing must reflect procurement lead times and regional supply volatility.
- Supportability: clear denial reasons and tooling for CS/SRE to explain behavior to customers.

files.description: PRD for the burst capacity option: user stories, requirements, non-goals, SLAs, pricing assumptions, rollout plan, and success metrics.
End-to-end design spec describing burst pool topology (by region/hardware), admission control, fairness model, and failure/rollback behavior.
ADR capturing key decisions: what constitutes a burst request, how denials are returned (queue vs immediate), and determinism guarantees.
ADR comparing fairness approaches (WFQ, token buckets, priority tiers) and selecting an implementation with measurable guardrails.
Fleet policy doc for sizing burst pools, safety margins, region constraints, and procurement implications.
Service doc for the burst admission controller: APIs, dependencies (policy engine, fleet telemetry), data model, and ownership.
Catalog of dashboards: burst saturation, denial reasons, per-tenant burst usage, and neighbor impact indicators (latency deltas).
SLO definitions and alert policy updates: what’s protected during burst, thresholds, paging rules, and error-budget gates for rollout.
Runbook for overload events: how to diagnose pool saturation, reduce caps, shift traffic, and communicate with Support/CS.
Game day plan to test guardrails: synthetic bursts, induced telemetry lag, routing failures, and rollback drills.
Packaging proposal: burst tiers, limits, metering approach, billing line items, and guidance for sales/CS.
Security/compliance doc specifying audit events for burst config changes, policy overrides, and administrative actions.
Working doc collecting customer pain points, peak patterns, and quotes from discovery calls; maps to PRD requirements.
Spreadsheet-style model estimating pool sizes from customer baselines, peak multipliers, utilization targets, and safety buffers.
Analysis notes on how bursts can affect tail latency; proposes detection metrics and candidate circuit breaker thresholds.
Informal design notes with pseudocode, state machines, and tricky edge cases (telemetry lag, retries, partial saturation).
Draft metric naming conventions, label cardinality constraints, and examples for burst-specific telemetry.
CS onboarding checklist for customers enabling burst: config validation, dashboards walkthrough, and escalation paths.
Sales enablement draft: what burst is, when to recommend it, common objections, and positioning vs competitors.
Rollout plan draft: regions/hardware order, capacity reservations, gating criteria, and rollback playbook links.
Finance model exploring margin impact under different burst utilization and pricing assumptions.
Post-beta retro notes capturing what broke, what guardrails were too strict/too lax, and action items for GA.
